messages:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a regression in tail latency after we flipped the new KV-prefix caching + kernel-selection patch on canary at ~15:02 UTC. Small spike but consistent across runs.

sanjay: which metrics are moving? token/p90 or p99?

mike: p95 and p99 moved. Quick counters from the canary run:
```
kernel_switch_count: 342 -> 890
avg_token_ms: 1.8 -> 2.4  (+33%)
prefill_hit_ratio: 0.62
batch_entropy: 0.47 -> 0.72
avg_batch_size_tokens: 224 -> 158
```
Seems like more heterogeneous batches are forming when prefix hits are high, causing kernels to thrash.

anya: interesting — caching reduced tokens per request but increased entropy inside the microbatch which forces kernel recompile/slow path. Did we change kernel selection thresholds?

mike: yes, the heuristic that picks the kernel now prefers the lowest-latency kernel per-request, but with mixed sequences it ends up switching mid-batch. That + smaller avg batch size => worse utilization.

cara: can we detect "batch heterogeneity" earlier and coalesce by homogeneity instead of raw token count? i.e., prefer slightly larger batch with same kernel vs many tiny mixed-kernel batches.

leah: proposal: add an "entropy_cap" to the batch planner that prevents forming a batch if estimated entropy > X OR else force a delayed-window to wait for more homogeneous arrivals. We can expose token_budget_target too.

mike: rough config I tried locally:
```
{"batch_homogeneity_threshold": 0.55, "entropy_cap_per_window": 0.6, "target_token_budget_ms": 120}
```
With that sim, avg_batch_size_tokens went up to 201 and avg_token_ms dropped to 1.9. p95 improved ~10%.

sanjay: nice. Where are we estimating entropy from? prefix-key variance + sequence-length distribution?

anya: current estimator: sample first N tokens' KV signatures per request (cheap hash) + length bucket. Compute normalized Shannon entropy over signature buckets per candidate batch window. Cheap and incremental.

cara: do we have numbers on kernel_switch_count reduction with the cap?

mike: sim run: kernel_switch_count 890 -> 410. Also saw steady GPU occupancy + fewer small kernel launches.

leah: potential downside: added latency for some cold requests due to waiting. Need a per-request SLA bypass (e.g., if latency budget < 60ms, bypass cap). Also need to tie to token_budget_target so we don't blow CPU timer.

sanjay: agree. Let's sketch the rollout plan:
- add entropy_cap config to canary runtime (non-default false)
- instrument extra counters: batch_entropy_hist, delayed_for_homogeneity, bypass_due_to_sla
- run AB on 5% traffic for 6 hours
- collect p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_count, occupancy, cost-per-token

mike: I'll open a PR with the planner change + instrumentation. Also adding a lightweight estimator in the client trace to validate hit vs miss correlation.

cara: we should also update kernel selection to prefer "stable" kernel for a short window if switching cost > threshold. Maybe introduce kernel_bias: prefer_stable=true as an orthogonal knob.

anya: good call. That will reduce oscillation without delaying requests. Combine both knobs for safety.

mike: PR attached when ready. Running local sim command I used: `./tools/sim_batcher --trace=kv_entropy --seed=17 --config=entropy_local.json`

leah: sounds good. Also please capture per-model behavior — some model archs tolerate heterogeneity better.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/canary v2.14.3 -> canary cluster (initiated by mike). ETA ~7m.

mike: started the canary run with entropy_cap=0.6, kernel_bias=prefer_stable. Will post early metrics in ~30m.

sanjay: thanks — if this looks good we'll keep config and roll to 25% with metric alarms.

cara: if this reduces cost-per-token we should fold into default packing heuristics and add doc in runtime/README about entropy estimator.

mike: quick note: sim results pinned in the PR but real traffic may differ because some customers have extremely short prefixes that skew buckets. We'll keep the bypass thresholds conservative.

leah: +1. Also add an e2e trace sample to perf dashboards so on-call can triage quickly.

mike: logged: follow-ups: 1) PR for entropy_cap, 2) kernel_bias flag, 3) instrumentation dashboards, 4) small AB plan. Will update thread.

cara: great — thanks! :thumbsup:
